chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gap Wood doesn't quit things. You see potential, you see a direction, and you'd rather build than walk away. In a situationship that instinct can keep you planting in soil that never agreed to be a garden. You tell yourself it's growing slowly, that they need time, that you'll know more next month. Sometimes that's true. Often you're staying because leaving would feel like admitting a project failed. Ask yourself plainly: am I here because this feels good now, or because I've already invested so much? Those are very different reasons, and only one of them is about joy.
chapters.what-you-want: You probably know exactly what you want. You just haven't said it, because for Gap Wood saying it out loud means committing to the outcome. Try anyway, privately first. Write one sentence that starts with I want a relationship where, and finish it honestly. Exclusive? Plans beyond next weekend? Being introduced to their friends? Tall trees like clarity. Not knowing where something is heading is genuinely uncomfortable for you, and that discomfort is information. It's telling you that casual may not be what you signed up for, even if you said it was at the start.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You see so much potential in them, Gap. That's lovely.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Potential isn't a relationship. It's a pitch deck.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: It's okay to want something defined.

chapters.why-you-stay: Eul Wood is the vine, and vines wrap around whatever is nearby. In a situationship you adapt to their rhythm: when they text, when they're free, what they're ready for. You're so good at making things easy that you can stay a long time without noticing you're always the one adjusting. You stay because connection matters to you, and some connection feels better than none. That's human. But ask yourself one gentle question: do I feel more secure since this started, or less? Your honest answer tells you more than any of their texts ever could.
chapters.what-you-want: You might honestly not know what you want, because you've been tuned to what they want for a while. Eul Wood is excellent at reading the room and slower at reading itself. So try this: imagine they offered you anything at all. What would you ask for? A title, consistency, being invited to things, a plan every week? Notice what comes up first, before you edit it down to something reasonable. That first answer is your want. It's allowed to be bigger than what you currently have, and it's allowed to be said out loud.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You make everything so easy for them, Eul.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Maybe too easy. When did they last adjust anything for you?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your want is allowed to be bigger than this.

chapters.why-you-stay: Byeong Fire is the sun, and you love the fun parts: the spark, the late calls, the inside jokes nobody else gets. A situationship can be all highlights and no responsibility, and honestly that's enjoyable for a while. You stay because when it's good, it's really good. But suns need warmth back too. If you've noticed you're giving more energy than you're getting, the fun can start to feel like a performance you're putting on twice a week. Ask yourself: if the fun nights stopped tomorrow, what would actually be left between you?
chapters.what-you-want: You know what you want, and you've probably already joked about it. Byeong Fire tends to say the true thing as a joke so it doesn't land too heavily. Haha, so are we dating or what. Try saying it without the haha. You want to be seen and celebrated, chosen in public and not only enjoyed in private. You want someone who's proud to stand next to your light. That's a completely reasonable thing to want, and you're allowed to want it now rather than at some vague point in the future.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: When it's good, it's so good. I get it, Byeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And when it's not, you just shine harder. Exhausting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say what you want without the joke.

chapters.why-you-stay: Jeong Fire is the candle, and when you connect, you connect deeply. Even an undefined thing feels intimate to you, because you bring your whole attention to it. You stay because the moments feel so real: the late talks, the small details they remember, the rare feeling of being understood. The question is whether that intimacy runs in both directions, or whether you're doing most of the feeling and quietly calling it us. Your depth is a gift. Make sure it's being received, not just enjoyed from a comfortable distance.
chapters.what-you-want: Being special to them is what you want, in a clear and steady way. Jeong Fire doesn't do half-attachments well, and you probably already feel more than you've admitted to anyone, including yourself. Write it down honestly: what would make you feel safe here? Consistent contact, knowing you're the only one, a simple name for what this is? Owning that want isn't needy. It's accurate. A candle needs a still room to burn well, and wanting stillness is not too much to ask of someone you're close to. Say it to yourself first, in a full sentence, so it sounds familiar when you say it to them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You bring so much depth to this, Jeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And they bring... a heart emoji every four days.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Wanting to feel special isn't needy.

chapters.why-you-stay: Mu Earth is the mountain: patient, steady, slow to move. In a situationship you wait. You assume things will settle into a shape if you just keep being reliable. At first you may not even mind the low pressure, since it asks nothing dramatic of you. You stay because leaving would require a decision you haven't fully made, and because you're loyal even to things without a name. Ask yourself one practical question: am I waiting for something specific to happen, or am I just waiting because waiting is what I do?
chapters.what-you-want: You want stability, someone you can actually count on. Mu Earth rarely says that out loud, because you'd rather show it than ask for it. You show up, you keep your word, you remember things. But being reliable yourself doesn't automatically make the other person reliable back. Name your want plainly: consistent plans, exclusivity, someone who shows up when it matters and not only when it's convenient. If that isn't happening, more patience from you is not the fix. It's simply more of the same. Wanting it doesn't make you demanding. It makes you clear about the foundation you'd build on.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You've been so patient and steady, Mu.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Patient, or just not deciding? Be honest.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Wanting stability is reasonable.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gi Earth is the garden, and you nurture whatever is in front of you. In a situationship you probably give a lot: you listen, you help, you remember things, you make every evening cozy. You stay because caring is your way of loving, and because part of you hopes that enough care will eventually turn this into something real. Ask yourself, gently but honestly: is this growing because of us, or only because of me? If you stopped watering it for two weeks, would anything still be standing? That question can sting a little. Answer it anyway, quietly, just for yourself.
chapters.what-you-want: You want to be taken care of too. Gi Earth often forgets to put that on the list at all. Think practically for a moment: what would care from them actually look like? Checking in on a hard day, making the plan for once, showing up when you're stressed without being asked. You're allowed to want a partner who tends your garden as well as their own. It's not asking too much. It's asking for even, which is the minimum for anything you'd call a relationship. Write down three small acts of care you'd love to receive. Specifics make it easier to notice when they're missing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You make everything so warm for them, Gi.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Unpaid caretaking for someone who won't commit. Love that for you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're allowed to want care back.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gyeong Metal is the blade, direct and loyal. Honestly, situationships aren't your natural habitat, because you like things clear and labeled. So if you're in one, something about this person got past your defences. You might be staying out of pride, not wanting to be the one who cares more first. Or you said casual at the beginning, and you keep your word even when it no longer fits. Check whether that early promise still matches who you are now, or whether you're just being loyal to an old sentence.
chapters.what-you-want: You want clarity and loyalty, plainly. Gyeong Metal knows this about itself. You might have avoided saying it because asking feels like showing weakness, like handing over a point. It isn't. A direct question is your superpower, and you use it brilliantly everywhere else in your life. You want to know where you stand, and you want to stand somewhere solid. That's a completely fair want. Not asking doesn't make you cooler. It just keeps you in a gray zone you actively dislike. Say it the way you'd say anything else important to you: simply, calmly, and once, without decoration.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You care about honesty more than anything, Gyeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then why are you in a situationship? That's your opposite.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Asking where you stand isn't weakness.

chapters.why-you-stay: Sin Metal is the jewel, refined and selective. You don't fall easily, so if you're in a situationship, this person impressed you. You might stay because you like the idea of them, or because asking for more feels like exposing yourself in an unflattering light. You'd rather be elegantly casual than visibly invested. Ask yourself honestly: is the casualness real, or is it a very beautiful cover for wanting something you're scared to ask for? Only you know, and you probably already do. Write the answer in one honest line, just for yourself. Nobody else needs to see it.
chapters.what-you-want: You want to be treasured. Seen in detail. Chosen with intention, not by default. Sin Metal has high standards, and that includes how you're treated by the people you let close. You may have lowered them temporarily to keep this light and easy. Write down what you'd want if you weren't worried about looking like too much. That list is your real standard, and it's not too high. It's simply specific, which is what good taste looks like when it's applied to love. Keep the list somewhere private and read it before your next date with them. See how it compares to what's actually happening.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You don't fall easily, Sin. They must have impressed you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And now you're pretending to be casual. Elegantly. Badly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your standards are not too high.

chapters.why-you-stay: Im Water is the ocean, and you love your freedom. Honestly, a situationship can suit you for a while. No pressure, plenty of space, nobody asking where you are on a Saturday. You might stay because it's easy, or because defining it would feel like signing up for a cage. But check yourself here. Are you genuinely happy with how undefined it is, or are you avoiding the question because answering it would mean staying in one harbor for longer than you're used to? Both answers are allowed. Just make sure it's the real one.
chapters.what-you-want: You might want something deeper than you're admitting. Im Water often thinks it wants freedom, when what it really wants is freedom with someone. What would good commitment look like for you, in your own terms? Space to roam, with a home to come back to? Separate adventures and shared Sundays? Define your version without borrowing anyone else's template. It doesn't have to look like your friends' relationships or anything on a screen. It only has to fit you and one other person. Write it as three short lines. If you can't, that's a sign to sit with the question a little longer before you ask them anything.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You love your freedom, Im. That's real.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also love not answering hard questions. Also real.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Maybe you want freedom with someone.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gye Water is the rain, intuitive and gentle. You feel deeply and quietly, and a situationship lets you keep those feelings unspoken, which can feel safe. You might stay because you sense something real between you, a connection that doesn't need words. Or because asking would feel far too exposing. Ask yourself softly: is the mystery here romantic, or is it just unclear? Romantic mystery makes you feel more alive. Unclear makes you feel more anxious. You can tell the difference if you're honest. Put your hand on your chest, ask the question, and notice what comes up first.
chapters.what-you-want: You want emotional closeness, to be understood without having to explain every single thing. Gye Water hopes that other people will simply intuit what it needs. They won't, not fully, not even the kind ones. So write your want down plainly: I want to know where I stand. I want to feel safe. I want us to be a real thing with a name. Seeing it in words makes it real, and it makes it much easier to say out loud when the moment comes. Read it back to yourself a few times until it stops sounding scary and starts sounding simply true.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You feel so much, Gye, even when you don't say it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Exactly. You don't say it. They're not mind readers.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Writing your feelings down first is a great idea.
